I really wanted to like this game and just couldn't get with it. UI design is great, voice acting is quirky and the world has a great steampunk-space theme going for it.

I just couldn't connect with the gameplay at all. Combat was uninteresting. Enemy variety felt repetitive. Non-city areas were all pretty uninteresting. First tried getting into it years ago and couldn't stick with it. Tried it again after Starfield (which I would recommend over this) and this game felt much worse.

I've heard the sequel is better so maybe that one will land for me but I just couldn't get into the game after multiple attempts, despite really wishing that I loved it.

The Outer Worlds delivers a compelling story-driven experience, especially in story mode with both expansions, that I would confidently recommend to fans of choice-heavy sci-fi adventures.

Character creation stands out immediately with extensive options for appearance, perks, and skills, letting you experiment even if you are unsure of your playstyle. Later, resettable options make it easy to adapt builds for quests or evolving strategies, which keeps progression flexible and forgiving.

The open-world exploration shines as a highlight, you are mostly free to roam, but your chosen skills and perks create meaningful limits that encourage early planning around stealth, combat, or dialogue-focused playstyles. Weapons and armor feature unique designs, though they grow slightly repetitive over time, paired with captivating graphics and interactive environments that enhance immersion.

Companions add narrative flavor through interactions, but they are skippable without major penalties if you prefer solo play, a smart design choice. Your actions shape the story organically, with no hand-holding warnings about consequences like missing recruits after aggressive playthroughs. That said, more enterable buildings would elevate exploration further.

- Prevented an insidious machine uprising that would have ended all biological life
- Flaunted conventional medical insurance policy by administering healthcare as an out-of-network provider
- Employed a man who curiously has no connection to the British monarchy despite simultaneously reviling the French and being at odds with organised religion
- Saved a village from the dangers posed by unlicensed botanical life
- Saved a town from the dangers posed by near-virulent malnutrition and mercury poisoning
- Provided solicited dating advice to the least shy engineer I will ever meet (and new best friend)
- Indefinitely suspended the execution of a pyromaniacal psilocybin mushroom farmer, by leveraging the shame that would befall the woman who wants him dead if people ever found out about the time he motorboated her squishy parts

Side quests are useful and also add additional content to the end game, and your choices have both meaning and lasting effects on how individuals interact with you and how your story pans out. Overall a great game, 8.5/10.

I don't like giving long winded reviews, so i'll just get to the point and say it's mediocre. 

Story options are okay, but some quests feel unfinished and leave you feeling unsatisfied, even with the "best endings". Character build options are about what you'd expect, with each level giving you points toward an attribute, but Perks are useless most times, and the "flaw" system is dumb (and since perks are useless, there is no actual reason to take them). The story is it's strongest attribute, and it is insanely good. I would love to see a sequel, but only if they take the time to flesh out the game more. 

Lastly, if there is one solid way to reliably measure an RPG's worth, it's the modding community. And let me tell you: it's dead and buried.
I reluctantly tell you to play Starfield instead. At least you can mod the weird shit out.

The Outer Worlds is a short, but excellent Fallout type game. Although the game world is not large, it does an excellent job of presenting a far-ranging Sci-Fi universe. The game's content is concentrated; one never needs to look far to find something to do. Companion characters are entertainingly voice acted, and seem more life-like than typical FPS characters. Highly recommended!

The Outer Worlds is a first-person sci-fi RPG, similar in form to games like Fallout 3. The story and overall theme is a bureaucratic dystopia, which is used as a source of humor to balance out the rather large number of dead bodies you stumble across.

There are some open areas, but it's not really an open-world game. Not quite Fallout on rails, but close. Still, it's a bright, vibrant environment with odds and ends tucked into hidden corners.

Playing on the "normal" difficulty, the combat becomes straightforward pretty quickly. Blindly hosing enemies down with an assault rifle or LMG works fine. Stealth + melee is also viable, but not necessary.

If you like RPG games like FallOut, or Elder Scrolls, you will like this. Mix in the type of dark humor you would find from Borderlands, and you get The Outer Worlds. GREAT game. Fun story, Absolutely amazing looking worlds. If you have even a have decent machine, this game looks amazing, and honestly plays buttery smooth. I think this is one of the better games in the last few years given how smooth this game runs and how great it looks.

100% worth checking out, even when at full price.

The world is tiny and empty. Locations are corridors, nothing to explore. You walk into a town and there's like ten NPCs, a couple of quests, that's it. No sense of a living world at all. Almost no lore either. The setting just doesn't grab you. Corporate satire boils down to "corporations bad, get it? get it?"
The humor everyone praises? Never found it.
Buy on a deep sale if you have absolutely nothing else to play.

This game has mixed reviews, and I can see why. After playing hundreds of hours in Fallout 4, I can see how this game seems to fall short in comparison.
Did I like this game - yes. It is now half off $15 - I paid $30 which I think is fair for how short the story line felt. If I had paid more, I would have been upset. It did feel a little lacking, and almost rushed? I don't know how to put this, but the trailers do not fit the game play at all. It makes it seem like there is so much possibility in the game of things to do, or factions but I didn't gather that. I saw in a previous review someone stated that this feels like a "fetch game" - not to spoil anything but all of the quests are either, go out and kill someone, or go get something.
Is the game worth playing, yes. But, it is a little disappointing as it could have had so much more potential. In the beginning of the game you have to choose what your job was/is and I thought that would have more impact then it actually did. I can also see how people feel it isn't very "open-world" because outside of very specific areas, there isn't anything to do. Also, all of the characters that you interact with, outside of the companions all looked the same. Hope this review helps! :)

It's set in the mid 24th century in an alternate universe in another star system called Halcyon. It is ruled by corporations. Sound familiar?
I won't go any further, since others have beaten me to it, so I will give you a useful bit of information about the two DLC add-ons: Peril on Gorgon and Murder on Eridanos.
Here it is.
In order to play the DLC, you must meet certain minimum player requirements. To play the Gorgon DLC, you must not be less than level 25 and you must have complete the Radio Free Monarch story quest. To play the Eridanos DLC, you must be at least level 30 and be able to visit Monarch. Given these criteria, you can play the Eridanos DLC BEFORE playing the Gorgon DLC, despite the Gorgon DLC being the first one released. It is possible to grind your way to level 30 before leaving Emerald Vale, which is roughly where you start the game.

A LOT changed between 2010 and 2020. Nearly all the elements that made Fallout New Vegas great, like the witty dialogue, intricate multi-faction plot intervowen with rich, charming and realistic characters, fully fleshed out RPG system with notable perks, and large variety of items supporting many gameplay styles. All of it missing in the Outer Worlds: A simplistic story with lifeless one note characters, boring itemization scheme, monotonous gameplay, and most importantly, no sense of humor.

While I don't think it was exceptional nor particularly ambitious, I think that works to its benefit. It's a solid story in a neat presentation and well-developed characters, even if they aren't immediately as interesting as a game like Mass Effect or even New Vegas.

Plus, one of the characters is outwardly ace and I thought that was pretty cool (and very rare) representation.
This is basically Bioshock in space, but with a little more humor thrown in. It's visually stunning. The characters are amazing.

I very much wish there were a neutral rating to give to this game. It wasn't bad, but it sure wasn't good. The gameplay was fine, but many of the design decisions led to a game that left you wishing you were playing something better.

Problems:
-Loot was built in such an absurd way. Too much health items to do effects that were a waste to manage. Choices for weapons were largely on rails without enough choices.
-Lack of depth with the story was a big problem. Quests were largely fetch or kill quest and most of the reasons for doing them felt empty and silly.
-Exploration felt so empty

Good things:
-Gunplay was very fun and engaging
-The tounge-in-cheek story was worth a few laughs.

Cons: Extremely short, this is the main reason i dont give 5 starts. Less than 18h for 1 char when i explored like crazy & was afk so in reality much less than 18h the 2nd run could prob be done in less than 4h including the side quests.
The lighting is rly bad when creating the char.
The companions & ada wont ever shut up, so i wish there was a mute option.
You have to return to the ship to switch companions.
No auto walk button which is very annoying when you're encumbered.
The looting is extremely annoying, you cant loot even when in range & looking directly at items sometimes, you have to walk up to it & spam e to find an angle to loot despite nothing being in the way so now my finger hurts.
